binders: There exists a real constant C.
Universally quantify over every type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
Universally quantify over every measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance.
Universally quantify over every real-valued function X : Ω → Real.
hypotheses: For the universally quantified X, LocalDef001 μ X holds: X is measurable and there exists K : Real with K > 0 such that exp(X(ω)^2/K^2) is μ-integrable and has integral at most 2 (with measurability and positivity repeated inside LocalDef004).
conclusions: The centered function ω ↦ X(ω) - ∫ x, X(x) dμ again satisfies LocalDef001 μ: it is measurable and has some positive real exponential-square scale whose exponential integral is at most 2.
The infimal admissible ENNReal scale of the centered function is at most ENNReal.ofReal C times the infimal admissible ENNReal scale of X.
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued function Y, define the real-scale exponential-square condition at K by: Y is measurable, K > 0, ω ↦ exp(Y(ω)^2/K^2) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(Y(ω)^2/K^2) dμ ≤ 2.
LocalDef001 μ Y means that Y is measurable and the real-scale exponential-square condition holds for at least one real K > 0.
For t : ENNReal, call t admissible for Y when Y is measurable, t ≠ 0, t ≠ ∞, ω ↦ exp(Y(ω)^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most 2.
Define the ENNReal-valued gauge of Y as inf {t : ENNReal | t is admissible for Y}.
Define the centered function Y(ω) = X(ω) - ∫ X dμ.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real constant C ≥ 1 such that, on every probability space and for every measurable real-valued function X having some positive scale K with integrable exponential square moment ∫ exp(X^2/K^2) dμ ≤ 2, subtracting the mean preserves that property, and the infimum of all finite nonzero ENNReal scales satisfying the same exponential-square bound for X - ∫X dμ is no larger than C times the corresponding infimum for X. The same C works independently of Ω, μ, and X.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement applies only under LocalDef001 μ X, which explicitly requires measurability and existence of a positive real exponential-square scale with an integrable exponential and integral at most 2.
The measure is restricted by an IsProbabilityMeasure instance; this is not a statement for arbitrary finite or σ-finite measures.
The constant C is merely asserted to exist with C ≥ 1; no numerical value, optimality, or dependence proof is encoded, although its quantifier position makes it uniform over all Ω, μ, and X.

The centering integral is the total Lean Bochner-integral operation. Integrability of X itself is not an explicit hypothesis in the target, although it is expected to follow mathematically from the exponential-square hypothesis on a probability space.
The gauge infimum ranges only over ENNReal scales t with t ≠ 0 and t ≠ ∞, and uses t.toReal in the denominator; hence every admissible denominator is finite and positive.

The infimum need not itself be an admissible scale and may equal 0. For a function with no admissible scales the definition can take the ENNReal infimum of the empty set, namely ∞; the antecedent is expected to provide admissible finite scales, but nonemptiness and finiteness are not separate conjuncts in the conclusion's inequality.

If an original gauge were ∞, the right side of the inequality could become ∞ and the bound would be uninformative; the LocalDef001 hypothesis is intended to rule this out through existence of a finite real witness, but that consequence is not stated separately.
ENNReal.ofReal clips negative real inputs to zero, but the constraint C ≥ 1 ensures the chosen C embeds as an ordinary positive finite ENNReal.

Measurability is pointwise Borel measurability of the displayed representatives, not merely an almost-everywhere measurability condition, while Integrable uses almost-everywhere strong measurability internally.

The theorem encodes neither symmetry nor a pre-existing zero-mean assumption on X, and it concludes no tail bound, moment bound, equality of gauges, or converse implication beyond the two displayed centering conclusions.
ambiguities: No material ambiguity remains in the proposition after expanding LocalDef001 through LocalDef006. The packet exposes MeasureTheory.integral through its type and a wrapped implementation rather than unfolding the wrapper, so its precise totalized behavior outside integrable inputs is not derivable from the body shown; this does not obscure the displayed use as the real Bochner integral, and the exponential-square premise is expected to imply integrability of X.
